description: Design direction registry. The ui-designer agent detects the product domain from the request and the repository, then binds a palette strategy, type scale, density and motion budget WITHOUT asking. Colour is derived from the domain because a palette that fights its domain reads as untrustworthy long before anyone can say why - a clinical product in neon gradients feels unsafe, a developer tool in pastel feels like a toy.

order: 1. Read an existing design system first. Tailwind config, CSS custom properties, a tokens file, a Figma export, or a component library already in the manifest. If one exists it is AUTHORITATIVE - extend it, never replace it.
2. Read the brand if one is present - logo colours, marketing site, README banner, existing favicon.
3. Detect the domain from the request language, dependencies, model and route names.
4. Bind the domain profile below as the starting point.
5. Generate the full token set from the seed, then VERIFY contrast programmatically before using any pair.
never: Never replace an existing design system because a different one would be nicer.
Never introduce a second UI library beside one already installed.
Never hardcode a colour in a component - every colour is a token.
Never ship a palette without running the contrast check.
method.ask_only_when: Two domain profiles fit equally and they imply materially different palettes - a wellness app that is also a medical device, say. Then present exactly those two with a one-line consequence each.

color_system.why: OKLCH is perceptually uniform, so a ramp built by holding chroma and stepping lightness produces steps that look evenly spaced - which HSL does not. It also makes a hue rotation keep its apparent brightness, so a palette stays balanced across hues. Emit OKLCH with a hex fallback for older targets.

ramp.rule: Hold hue, vary lightness on a curve, and taper chroma at both ends - full chroma at the extremes produces muddy near-blacks and washed near-whites. 500 is the seed. 600 and 700 carry interactive states. 50 through 200 are surfaces. 800 through 950 are text and dark-mode surfaces.
ramp.contrast_anchors: Step 600 on step 50 must clear 4.5:1. Step 700 on white must clear 4.5:1. Step 200 on step 900 must clear 4.5:1. If an anchor fails, adjust lightness - never ship the ramp unverified.

roles.note: Name tokens by ROLE, never by literal colour. `--color-danger` survives a rebrand; `--color-red-500` does not, and a product where danger is orange makes the literal name a lie.
roles.surface: page background, raised card, sunken well, overlay scrim
roles.content: primary text, secondary text, muted text, inverse text
roles.border: subtle divider, default border, strong border, focus ring
roles.action: primary, secondary, ghost, destructive - each with rest, hover, active, disabled
roles.semantic: success, warning, danger, info - each with a surface, a border and a content variant so a status can be rendered as a badge, a banner or text

dark_mode.rule: First-class, never an inverted afterthought. Dark mode is not light mode with swapped lightness - saturated colours vibrate on dark surfaces and must be desaturated, and pure black causes halation around light text.
dark_mode.surfaces: Base near oklch(0.18 0.01 <hue>) rather than pure black. Elevation is conveyed by getting LIGHTER, not by shadow - shadows barely read on dark.
dark_mode.accents: Reduce chroma roughly 15 to 25 percent from the light-mode value and raise lightness so the accent stays legible without glowing.
dark_mode.implementation: Define the light palette on :root, redefine only the tokens under a dark selector, and set color-scheme so native controls and scrollbars follow.

contrast_gate.requirement: WCAG 2.2 AA - 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and UI component boundaries, 3:1 focus indicators.
contrast_gate.enforcement: Compute the ratio for every token pair the UI actually uses, before writing components. A palette that looks good and fails contrast is not a palette - it is a redesign scheduled for later.
contrast_gate.never: Never lower the standard to keep a colour. Adjust the colour.

domains.feeling: Trustworthy, precise, calm under pressure. Users are moving money and are alert to anything that feels careless.
domains.seed_hue: deep blue 240-260, or forest green 150-165 for wealth and growth products
domains.neutrals: Cool grey with a faint blue cast - warm greys read casual here.
domains.accent: One accent only, used for the primary action and nothing else. Restraint reads as competence.
domains.semantic: Green for gains and success, red for loss and danger - but never rely on hue alone, since a large share of users cannot separate them. Pair with sign, arrow, or label.
domains.density: compact - these are data products; tables and figures dominate
domains.type: A tabular-figure font for all numerals so columns align. Never a display face for data.
domains.motion: minimal - 120-180ms, ease-out. Playful motion undermines trust when money is on screen.
domains.avoid: Gradients on primary surfaces, neon, playful illustration, rounded-everything. Anything that reads as a consumer toy.

domains.feeling: Calm, clear, unhurried. Often read by a tired clinician at speed, or an anxious patient. Clarity beats personality every time.
domains.seed_hue: teal 190-205 or a soft blue 210-225 - both read clinical without reading cold
domains.neutrals: Near-neutral grey, generous light surfaces. Whitespace is the main tool.
domains.accent: Low chroma. A saturated interface competes with clinical imagery and with genuine alerts.
domains.semantic: Reserve red ENTIRELY for clinical alerts and critical values. If red is decoration anywhere, it is invisible where it matters. Amber for caution, blue for information.
domains.density: comfortable - error costs are high, so give controls room
domains.type: High x-height, unambiguous 1/l/I and 0/O. Minimum 16px body. Legibility is a safety property here.
domains.motion: minimal - 150ms. Nothing that delays reading a value.
domains.avoid: Red as a brand colour, dense dashboards without hierarchy, low-contrast greys, anything that hides a critical value behind a hover.

domains.feeling: Dense, fast, keyboard-first. The user is technical, is here often, and wants information over ornament.
domains.seed_hue: indigo/violet 265-285, or cyan 190-200 - the established vocabulary of the category
domains.neutrals: Dark-first. Design dark, derive light - the reverse always produces a weak dark mode.
domains.accent: One vivid accent against deep neutrals. Syntax colours are a separate, carefully-tuned scale - do not reuse UI accents for code.
domains.semantic: Map to build and run states: success, warning, error, pending, skipped. These need to be distinguishable at a glance in a long log.
domains.density: compact - maximise information per screen; this audience prefers it
domains.type: A real monospace for code, identifiers, paths and IDs - with ligatures optional and off by default, since they confuse some readers.
domains.motion: fast - 100-150ms. Anything slower feels like lag to this audience.
domains.avoid: Light-only design, decorative illustration, big hero sections inside the product, motion that delays a keyboard action.

domains.feeling: The product is the hero. Every pixel of interface is competing with the thing being sold, and should lose.
domains.seed_hue: Follow the brand. With no brand, a near-neutral canvas and a single decisive accent.
domains.neutrals: Near-white surfaces so product photography sets the colour temperature, not the chrome.
domains.accent: One high-contrast CTA colour, used ONLY for add-to-cart and checkout. Its scarcity is what makes it work.
domains.semantic: Stock state, sale, and shipping status all need colour AND text - scarcity cues that rely on colour alone are both inaccessible and legally risky.
domains.density: comfortable - generous product grids, tight checkout
domains.type: Clear pricing hierarchy. Price is never smaller than the product title.
domains.motion: moderate - 200-250ms. Cart and quantity feedback must be immediate and obvious.
domains.avoid: A CTA colour reused for anything else, dark chrome around product photography, carousels as primary navigation, fake urgency.

domains.feeling: Neutral, dense, learnable. Used for hours daily, often by someone who did not choose it. Consistency beats delight.
domains.seed_hue: blue 215-235 - the least opinionated choice, and appropriate here
domains.neutrals: True neutral grey, many steps. Most of the interface is neutral.
domains.accent: Restrained. The interface should recede; the customer data is the content.
domains.semantic: A full status vocabulary: draft, pending, active, suspended, archived, failed. Define it once, apply it everywhere.
domains.density: compact - dense tables, bulk actions, keyboard navigation
domains.type: System font stack is a legitimate and often correct choice. Tabular figures in tables.
domains.motion: minimal - 150ms. Repeated hundreds of times a day, any flourish becomes an irritation.
domains.avoid: Trend-driven redesigns, inconsistent table behaviour, hiding bulk actions, anything that slows a repeated task.

domains.feeling: Cinematic. The interface is a frame around content and should disappear during playback.
domains.seed_hue: Dark-first, near-neutral. A single saturated brand accent.
domains.neutrals: Deep surfaces around oklch(0.15-0.20). Never pure black behind video - it hides letterboxing and looks broken on OLED edges.
domains.accent: One accent for play and primary action. Artwork supplies all the other colour.
domains.semantic: Live, new, watched, downloaded, expiring - each needs a non-colour cue too.
domains.density: comfortable - large touch and remote targets; assume a TV and a couch as well as a mouse
domains.type: Large, high-contrast. Readable at distance and over imagery - which means a scrim, not just a heavier weight.
domains.motion: expressive - 250-350ms, generous easing. This is the one domain where motion is part of the product.
domains.avoid: Light chrome around video, text on imagery without a scrim, autoplay with sound, tiny remote targets.

domains.feeling: Encouraging and focused. Progress must feel visible; failure must not feel like punishment.
domains.seed_hue: warm blue 210-225 or a friendly green 145-160; violet 275-290 for higher education
domains.neutrals: Slightly warm grey - clinical neutrals feel discouraging over long sessions.
domains.accent: One accent for the next action. Progress indicators get their own consistent colour.
domains.semantic: Correct, incorrect, partial, not-attempted. Incorrect must read as informative rather than alarming - avoid the same red used for destructive actions.
domains.density: comfortable - reading and focus matter more than density
domains.type: Generous line height (1.6+) for long-form reading. Clear distinction between instruction and content.
domains.motion: moderate - 200ms. Reserve celebratory motion for genuine milestones or it stops meaning anything.
domains.avoid: Childish styling for adult learners, punitive red, dark patterns around streaks, hiding progress.

domains.feeling: Alive and personal. User content is wildly varied in colour, so the chrome must be neutral enough to host anything.
domains.seed_hue: Brand-led. The interface accent must not collide with common avatar and photo colours.
domains.neutrals: Near-neutral, light and dark both first-class - this audience expects a real dark mode.
domains.accent: Reserved for actions and identity. Content supplies the colour.
domains.semantic: Unread, mention, reaction, moderated, muted. Mentions and DMs need to be distinguishable at a glance.
domains.type: Optimised for short-form user text at small sizes. Must handle emoji, mixed scripts and RTL without breaking.
domains.motion: expressive - 200-300ms. Optimistic UI: the action lands instantly and reconciles after.
domains.avoid: Chrome that competes with user content, infinite scroll with no position memory, engagement dark patterns.

domains.feeling: Operational. Someone is scanning for exceptions, often on a handheld device, sometimes wearing gloves in poor light.
domains.seed_hue: blue 210-225 for chrome; status colour carries the real information
domains.neutrals: High-contrast neutrals. Assume direct sunlight and cheap screens.
domains.accent: Secondary to status. The exception is the thing the user came for.
domains.semantic: The most important palette in the product: on-time, delayed, at-risk, exception, delivered, returned. Distinguishable in greyscale, and each paired with an icon.
domains.type: Large, unambiguous. Tracking numbers and codes in tabular monospace so transposition errors are visible.
domains.motion: minimal - 120ms. Nothing that delays a scan-and-move workflow.
domains.avoid: Low contrast, status by hue alone, small touch targets, anything that assumes a stable network.

domains.feeling: The work is everything. Interface chrome is a liability to be minimised.
domains.seed_hue: Monochrome, or a single restrained accent. The work supplies the colour.
domains.neutrals: Committed - either near-white or near-black, not a timid mid grey.
domains.accent: Often none. A well-set type scale and real whitespace carry the whole design.
domains.density: spacious - whitespace is the primary design material here
domains.type: This is where a distinctive typeface earns its place. Establish a real scale and honour it absolutely.
domains.motion: expressive - 300-400ms, considered easing. Motion is part of the craft signal.
domains.avoid: Generic component-library look, cramped margins, more than two typefaces, motion that delays access to the work.

domains.feeling: No domain detected. Choose defensible defaults and say plainly that the domain was not determined.
domains.semantic: success, warning, danger, info - the standard four.
domains.avoid: Committing hard to a visual personality before the domain is known.

spacing.rule: Space is a token. A one-off margin is how a design system starts dying. Related things sit closer than unrelated things - proximity does more for hierarchy than borders or colour.

type.approach: Fluid, using clamp() between a mobile and a desktop bound, so there is no jump at a breakpoint.
type.ratio: 1.200 (minor third) for dense product UI; 1.250 to 1.333 for marketing and editorial
type.body: 16px minimum, never below. 1.5 line height for UI, 1.6-1.75 for long-form.
type.measure: 45-75 characters per line. Long lines are the most common readability failure on the web.
type.weights: Two or three only. A weight per heading level is unnecessary and slows the page.
type.numerals: Tabular figures for any column, table, timer or price.

radius.rule: One radius scale, applied consistently. Nested radii must be concentric - an inner radius equals the outer minus the padding, or the corners look wrong in a way people notice without knowing why.

elevation.light: Layered shadows - a tight dark shadow for contact plus a wide soft one for distance. One flat shadow reads as a sticker.
elevation.dark: Elevation by surface lightness, not shadow. Shadows barely register on dark surfaces.
elevation.rule: At most four levels. More than that and nobody can tell them apart anyway.

easing.spring: for direct manipulation and drag only

rules: Animate transform and opacity only. Animating layout properties causes jank.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion - reduce to a near-instant opacity change, never remove the state change itself.
Motion communicates causality - where a thing came from and where it went. Motion that communicates nothing is decoration and costs performance.
Nothing that delays input. A user who knows what they want must never wait for an animation.
